# Methods

*Study design and team status*

This capstone is being completed as an individual project. As such, all data acquisition, processing, modeling, and interpretations will be produced soley by the author.

All data analysis and processing will be performed using the R programming language [@r]. Environmental observation data will be acquired from the EPA's Water Quality Portal via the dataRetrieval r-package [@wqp_2026; @dataRetrieval2026]. Data QA/QC and preprocessing will be completed utilizing the Tidyverse package and any spatially aware data processing will be conducted using the package sf [@tidyverse; @sf]. *Study Area*

The study area for this project is the Pensacola Bay System which includes portions of Pensacola Bay, Escambia Bay, East Bay and Blackwater Bay. Boundaries of this study area were achieved by accessing Florida Department of Protections (FDEP) Waterbod IDs feature layer hosted on ArcGIS Online [@FDEP2005WBIDs]. Once retrieved, the dataset was filtered to include only relevant WBIDs (WBID = 548) and then combined to create a singular study area polygon. Creating the study area polygon is an important first step as it will be needed to extract relevant environmental data from much larger datasets in the coming data gathering. The study area was intentionally chosen in an attempt to match the previous study area applied in @Geselbracht2024. 

![Study area for the Pensacola Bay System.](4-tables-and-figures/study-area.png){#fig-study-area}

*Data acquisition and dataset inventory*

Oyster occurence data was acquired from the Florida Fish and Wildlife Commission's GIS portal as polygons and converted to points using polygon centroids. After clipping to the study area extent, ### known reef locations were present within the PBS [@FWC2026Oysters]. Salinity, dissolved oxygen, temperature, and turbidity, and chlorophyll-a observations were obtained from the Water Quality Portal using the 'dataRetrieval' package in R for all sites located within the PBS and collected within the 20 year period from 2005 to 2025 [@wqp_2026, @dataRetrieval2026]. Parameters were chosen based on relevance and represenation in previous oyster habitat retoration studies [@LaPeyre2021; @Barnes2007; @Pollack2012; @Geselbracht2024]. Bathymetry data for the PBS was obtained from NOAA as a #### resolution raster dataset [@NOAA_2018]. ***DOES BATHYMETRY DATA NEED TO BE RESAMPLED TO NEW CELL SIZE?***. Substrate data was obtained from the Pensacola and Perdido Bay Estuary Program and was the same dataset used in their earlier HSI study which was modeled on the @Geselbrach2024 study.

**Water-quality Data Preprocessing**

All water quality parameters were inspected to ensure comparable measurement units and analytical procedures and avoid combining different forms of similar analytes. Further, to maintain consistency with other similar oyster studies, all data was filtered to only include warm season conditions. Here, the warm season is defined as May through October. Finally, the data was screened for any extreme outliers, where outliers were defined as:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Outlier if } \quad
x &< Q_{0.25} - 1.5(IQR) \\
\text{or} \quad
x &> Q_{0.75} + 1.5(IQR) \\
\\
\text{where } IQR &= Q_{0.75} - Q_{0.25}
\end{aligned}
$$

Following data cleaning, station-level environmental summaries were calculated to represent warm-season conditions that could be expected at that station. Stations that only had one sample were also removed as it was considered one sample was not representitive enough to be considered the normal conditions over the full 20 year period. Finally, the station-level dataset was converted to spatial using the `sf` package in r and projected to NAD 1983 (2011) StatePlane Florida North FIPS 0903 in meters [@sf].
